solver: V1.0 Go Gurobi-MIP decomposition outer loop (cmd/solve): global hot-cell decompose (hot-k=6), per-demand waypoint candidates, lexicographic peeling MIP (peel=6), accept only on real truncated-lex improvement, Hamming-budget rows, sticky pool model. New in this experiment: a one-shot presolve phase (15s global budget, run once at solve start) that records, for every (slot, arc) cell with positive load, a sound *load floor* = volume of the demands that structurally cannot avoid the arc (class 1 bridges, class 2 sink/source dominance, class 3 exact per-demand dodge test). Floors feed (a) the MIP as >= rows, (b) layer-0 zlb via SatFloor, (c) an optional -skip-floor round-seed filter, (d) a final first-bit certificate.

presolve_semantics.floor_vs_pin: load(t,e) >= sum_{d in F} vol_d(t) holds for EVERY routing (a floor). lb==ub (a full pin) additionally requires that no other demand can ever reach e; the early rule 'sum forced == observed load -> pin' was unsound and was replaced by the noNewUser test (source unreachable / target unreachable / w(e) > dist(u,v)).
presolve_semantics.proven_pins: 0 on every setA and setB instance, by design (ning lou wu cuo: rather miss than be wrong). Revoked = 0, no pin-violation WARN.
presolve_semantics.lb_sat: LB_sat = max over all recorded floors of floor/cap; its trunc6 is a lower bound on the first bit of the sorted saturation vector.

bench_binaries.note: the four A/B arms ran concurrently in the same time window so every instance pair shares identical CPU contention

coverage.note: setA-16..20 and part of setA-13..15 did not finish inside the experiment time box: -wall-sec is only checked between rounds and one MIP round can run 30+ minutes on the hard instances (off arm: setA-16 nominal 90s, actual 3020s). All cross-arm comparisons in the report use the 12 instances common to all four arms.

objective: saturation (arc x slot) loads flattened, sorted descending, trunc6 lexicographic (smaller better); layer 1 = max saturation (MLU)
